chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Abd al-Samad ibn Muhammad, from Hanan, from his father, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
If you enter a town and say, “Today I will leave,” or “Tomorrow I will leave,” then you remain for a full month, then perform fully.

key_terms.أَخْرُجُ: I leave; expressing the expectation of imminent departure
key_terms.الْبَلَدَ: the town or locality entered by the traveler
key_terms.شَهْرًا: a month; the legal period mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.فَأَتِمَّ: then perform fully; i.e., complete the salat rather than shortening it
key_terms.فَاسْتَتْمَمْتَ: then you completed or fulfilled; meaning the stay reached its full measure

ai.seo_question: When must a traveler start performing full prayers if he stays in a town without knowing how long he will remain?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a traveler who enters a town without knowing how long he will stay, while intending to leave soon day by day. If this state continues until a full month is completed, he must thereafter perform the prayer in full.
